This petition is filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 by the petitioner/accused No.5 for grant of bail in Crime No.115/2022 dated 29.11.2022 by the Janwada Police, Bidar Rural, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 366-A, 376(2)(n), 376(3) 384, 107, 109, 114 and 506 r/w Section 149 of IPC, Sections 4, 6, 12 and 17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for brevity "POCSO Act") and Section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2016, presently pending on the file of Addl. Dist. & Sessions Judge at Bidar.

sentences.text: NC: 2026:KHC-K:829 HC-KAR 2.
The factual matrix of the case is that the elder daughter of respondent No.2 was aged about 15 years and was studying in SSLC at Bidar and she used to commute for School from her native.
On the night of 24.11.2022, when respondent No.2 and the family members were sleeping, it was observed that respondent No.2's daughter/victim was missing.
Upon search of two days, they failed to trace her.
As such, on suspicion, they lodged the complaint against accused No.1 before respondent- Police, which registered in Crime No.115/2022 for the offence punishable under Section 366-A of IPC.
Subsequently, accused No.1 and victim were traced on 01.12.2022 and on enquiry it was revealed that accused No.1 kidnapped her and taken her to Mumbai and other accused helped accused No.1.
Accordingly, this petitioner implicated in the crime by arraying as accused No.5.

Later, the respondent-Police have filed charge sheet against the petitioner and others by invoking Sections 363, 366, 366- A, 376(2)(n), 376(3) 384, 107, 109, 114 and 506 r/w NC: 2026:KHC-K:829 HC-KAR Section 149 of IPC, Sections 4, 6, 12 and 17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for brevity "POCSO Act") and Section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2016.

sentences.text: Subsequently, the case was set up for trial and three witnesses have been examined including the victim.
In the meantime, the petitioner-accused No.5, failed to appear before the Trial Court.
As such, the learned Special Judge issued warrant against him and cancelled the bail granted to him and the bond amount was forfeited.
Accordingly, the petitioner was sent to judicial custody on 11.11.2025.
Ever since, he is in custody.

Thereafter, the petitioner approached the Addl. Dist. &
Sessions Judge, Bidar, in Crl.Misc.No.571/2025, which was dismissed vide order dated 15.12.2025.
Hence, this petition.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:829 HC-KAR 4.
I have given my anxious consideration both on the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the documents available on record.
5. As could be gathered from records, the petitioner was already granted bail in Crl.Misc.No.569/2023 and subsequently, the prosecution has examined three witnesses including the victim.
All the three witnesses have turned hostile to the prosecution case.
No doubt, this petitioner has violated the bail conditions and failed to appear before the Trial Court.

However,
since the victim herself turned hostile to the prosecution case, the further custodial incarceration of the petitioner/accused No.5 does not call for.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
